content: It includes information about the authors, publication years, titles, journals, and reasons for exclusion or inclusion in a systematic review. 1. Gamboa et al. (2009) investigated the relationship between geohelminth infections and socio-environmental conditions across different human populations in Argentina. Their findings were published in the Pan American Journal of Public Health, Volume 26, Issue 1, pages 1–8. 2. Garcia et al. (2013) explored family feeding practices in children aged 0–4 years with preventable pathologies. This study was documented in the Annals of Nutrition and Metabolism, Volume 63, page 1035. 3. Gbary et al. (2011) analyzed the epidemiological and clinical aspects of the cholera outbreak in the Littoral department of Benin in 2008. The results were published in Médecine Tropicale, Volume 71, Issue 2, pages 157–161. 4. Karmakar et al. (2008) conducted an epidemiological analysis of a post-earthquake outbreak of rotavirus gastroenteritis in Kashmir, India. Their findings were published in Public Health, Volume 122, Issue 10, pages 981–989. 5. Khosla et al. (2005) emphasized the importance of sanitation as a resource for promoting urban child health. This study appeared in Indian Pediatrics, Volume 42, Issue 12, pages 1199–1206. 6. Masoumeh et al. (2012) examined intestinal parasitic infections among schoolchildren in Golestan Province, Iran. Their research was published in the Pakistan Journal of Biological Sciences, Volume 15, Issue 23, pages 1119–1125. 7. Molina et al. (2011) reported a high prevalence of Giardia intestinalis genotype B infections among children in both urban and rural areas of Argentina. This study was published in the Annals of Tropical Medicine & Parasitology, Volume 105, Issue 4, pages 299–309. 8. Monasta et al. (2008) conducted a case study on the living conditions and health of children in five foreign Roma camps in Italy. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Public Health, Volume 98, Issue 11, pages 2035–2041. 9. Ostan et al. (2007) highlighted health inequities, showing that lower socioeconomic conditions are associated with higher incidences of intestinal parasites. This study was published in BMC Public Health, Volume 7, Article A99342. 10. Sanchez et al. (2004) used brachial and cephalic perimeters as indicators of poverty and acute diarrhea in children under five years in Bogotá. Their findings were published in Revista de Salud Pública, Volume 6, Issue 2, pages 167–182. 11. Sanchez-Uribe et al. (2013) identified risk factors associated with rotavirus gastroenteritis during a community outbreak in Chiapas, Mexico, in the post-vaccination era. This study was published in the Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society, Volume 2, Issue 1, pages 15–20. 12. Semba et al. (2009) found that the purchase of drinking water was linked to increased child morbidity and mortality among urban slum-dwelling families in Indonesia. Their research was published in the International Journal of Hygiene & Environmental Health, Volume 212, Issue 4, pages 387–397. 13. Wells and Harris (2007) explored the relationship between housing quality, psychological distress, and social withdrawal in low-income women. Their longitudinal study was published in the Journal of Environmental Psychology, Volume 27, Issue 1, pages 69–78. 14. Bask (2011) examined the cumulative disadvantage and its connections to welfare problems. This study was published in Social Indicators Research, Volume 103, Issue 3, pages 443–464. 15. Bright et al. (2013) investigated whether neighborhood poverty explains racial and ethnic differences in sleep duration. Their findings were presented in Circulation, Volume 127, Issue 12 (Meeting Abstracts). 16. Brown and Low (2008) studied the impact of chaotic living conditions and sleep problems on children's academic performance. Their research was published in the Journal of Family Psychology, Volume 22, Issue 6, pages 920–923. 17. Lianqi et al. (2004) analyzed sleep problems and related factors among elementary school students. Their findings were published in the Chinese Mental Health Journal, Volume 18, Issue 9, pages 613–616. 18. McGrath and Jarrin (2013) found that children's perception of neighborhood safety mitigates the effects of neighborhood disorder on sleep. Their study was published in Psychosomatic Medicine, Volume 75, Issue 3. 19. Umlauf et al. (2011) reported on sleep disturbances among disadvantaged minority teens. Their findings were published in Sleep, Volume 34, Article A299. 20. Ahmadzad-Asl et al. (2013) examined the correlates of mental health service utilization among married women in Tehran. Their findings were published in the Iranian Journal of Psychiatry & Behavioral Sciences, Volume 7, Issue 1, pages 51–60. 21. Al-Khatib et al. (2005) studied the housing environment and its impact on women's health in a Palestinian refugee camp. Their research was published in the International Journal of Environmental Health Research, Volume 15, Issue 3, pages 181–191. 22. Ambrose (2010) discussed the issue of overcrowding in housing. This study was published in Roof, Volume 35, Issue 2, pages 31–33. 23. Binbay et al. (2010) reported a high prevalence of psychosis continuum in a highly urbanized area of Turkey. Their findings were published in Schizophrenia Research, Volume 117, Issues 2–3, page 435. 24. Borders et al. (2007) examined the relationship between chronic stress and low birth weight neonates in a low-income population of women. Their study was published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, Volume 109, Issue 2, Part 1, pages 331–338. 25. Chen et al. (2014) explored the role of temperament and family environment interactions in child maladjustment. Their findings were published in the Journal of Abnormal Child Psychology, Volume 42, Issue 8, pages 1251–1262. 26. Coutinho et al. (2014) analyzed the prevalence of common mental disorders and their relationship to the social context in São Paulo. Their study was published in Cadernos de Saúde Pública, Volume 30, Issue 9, pages 1875–1883. 27. Drury et al. (2006) assessed housing space standards in Greater London. Their findings were published in a report for the Greater London Authority. 28. Eriksson et al. (2011) identified early risk factors for criminal offending in schizophrenia through a 35-year longitudinal cohort study. Their findings were published in Social Psychiatry & Psychiatric Epidemiology, Volume 46, Issue 9, pages 925–932. 29. Evans and Cassells (2014) examined the impact of childhood poverty and cumulative risk exposure on mental health in emerging adults. Their study was published in Clinical Psychological Science, Volume 2, Issue 3, pages 287–296. 30. Ferguson et al. (2013) reviewed the influence of the physical environment on child development. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Psychology, Volume 48, Issue 4, pages 437–468. 31. Fisher et al. (2007) studied the relationship between socioeconomic advantage and mood during advanced pregnancy in women in Vietnam. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Mental Health Systems, Volume 1, Article 3. 32. Fisher et al. (2011) emphasized the importance of recognizing maternal mental health in resource-constrained settings to achieve Millennium Development Goals. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Mental Health Systems, Volume 5, Article 2. 33. Gariepy et al. (2014) examined the relationship between neighborhood characteristics and the 10-year risk of depression in Canadian adults. Their findings were published in Health & Place, Volume 30, pages 279–286. 34. Grzywacz et al. (2010) studied depressive symptoms among Latino farmworkers across the agricultural season. Their findings were published in Cultural Diversity & Ethnic Minority Psychology, Volume 16, Issue 3, pages 335–343. 35. Guitte et al. (2006) analyzed the impact of the physical and urban environment on mental well-being. Their findings were published in Public Health, Volume 120, Issue 12, pages 1117–1126.
